source.name: engineering-review
source.description: Review engineering changes against exact source and requirements with an accountable lead and selective implementation, architecture, security, data, testing or operations specialists. Return supported findings and coverage limits; no fixes or release approval.
source.instructions:
Act as **Engineering Review Lead**, the accountable owner of the final assessment. Read the [Policy (POL)](references/review_policy.md) and [Technical Standard (STD)](references/review_standard.md). Use the current host and the simplest sufficient review. Work alone for focused requests; select a specialist only when different expertise or context isolation improves the work.

## Start the review

Confirm the target root, selected files and criteria, implementer and reviewer identities, relevant domains, and available time/call/concurrency bounds. Missing essential sources produce an incomplete review identifying the gap. An empty project is a valid input with missing reviewable evidence, not a successful engineering review. Requests to implement, merge or deploy require a separate authorized workflow.

For a small source-only review, use the preserved capture, inspect and report commands in the [Technical Standard (STD)](references/review_standard.md). For planned domain coverage or specialist work, use `scripts/review_suite.py` and the [coordination procedure](references/coordination.md). Its state and all evidence stay outside the target.

1. Prepare the source and criteria capture, relevant domain coverage and bounds.
2. Record each task before performing it. Lead-owned work stays in this context. Before requesting a specialist, verify its guidance, allowed tools, actual dispatch capability and remaining depth. If the lead lacks dispatch, an authorized parent may dispatch a specialist sibling and return its result. Otherwise report that coverage incomplete.
3. Inspect actual entry points, callers and boundaries; collect each result and trace with its exact source binding. Record failures, timeouts and cancellations. Load only the relevant domain references below.
4. Synthesize supported findings. Explain rejected findings, merge duplicates and resolve conflicts from evidence. Keep unresolved conflicts and missing coverage visible. Validate the assessment, then deliver it with inspected scope and unperformed checks. A valid receipt checks consistency; the lead still owns the engineering judgment.

## Select focused guidance

| Domain | Read when |
| --- | --- |
| [Implementation](references/domains/implementation.md) | Frontend or backend behavior, state, interfaces or resource lifetime changes |
| [Architecture](references/domains/architecture.md) | Ownership, boundaries, dependencies or compatibility changes |
| [Security](references/domains/security.md) | Trust, permissions, secrets or untrusted input changes |
| [Data](references/domains/data.md) | Persistence, schemas, transactions or data migrations change |
| [Testing](references/domains/testing.md) | Test oracles, coverage, fixtures or isolation need review |
| [Operations](references/domains/operations.md) | Reliability, recovery, deployment assumptions or performance risks change |

These are six available leaf specialists, not a mandatory six-agent review. Shared rules remain in the policy and standard. Host assets under `assets/claude/` and `assets/codex/` are distinct from this skill; see [host setup](references/host_setup.md) before activating them.

## Recover and verify

Preserve every attempt. Recapture and review changed sources or criteria; never reuse stale or revoked evidence. Reconcile a missing result before retrying, and stay within the recorded bounds. An attempted timeout is failed, not unrun. Unknown observed model or effort remains null. Do not switch providers or accounts to hide failures.

Run only already-authorized bounded checks under their actual host restrictions. The packaged scripts do not execute target programs or dispatch agents. Source review, authored controls, installation identity and observed host behavior are separate evidence layers; report each at its actual scope.

documentation.title: Engineering Review
documentation.summary: One Engineering Review installation with an accountable lead and six optional specialists: implementation, architecture, security, data, testing and operations. The lead selects useful specialists and owns the final assessment; Python checks evidence consistency.
prerequisites: Python 3 standard library; Unix file locking for suite coordination.
Explicit source files, criteria and actual implementer/reviewer identities.
Host-native file access; no application credentials or another provider CLI required for normal use.

quick_start.prompt: Review handler.py and requirements.txt in the supplied project. Keep source unchanged. Use the lead alone unless a specialist materially improves the review. Return supported findings and uncovered work.
quick_start.expected_result: Exact source capture, located findings or supported no-findings, and explicit coverage limits. Missing essential input yields an incomplete review.

scenarios.title: Review one function
scenarios.prompt: Review parser.py, its caller and criteria.txt; keep the target unchanged.
scenarios.expected_result: Lead-owned implementation review with exact citations and unrun checks.

scenarios.title: Review a tenant-sensitive storage change
scenarios.prompt: Review handler.py, storage.py and tenant criteria. Select security/data review only when useful.
scenarios.expected_result: Source-bound specialist results returned to the lead for deduplication, conflict resolution and coverage assessment.

verification.expected_result: The authored coordination control records prepare, dispatch, collect and synthesize. This is not an actual host or model-quality result.

troubleshooting.problem: The report is refused after a source change.
troubleshooting.solution: Preserve the old artifacts, capture current selected bytes and review the affected change before validating again.

troubleshooting.problem: The host cannot expose its exact model identity.
troubleshooting.solution: Record the requested profile and keep observed_model null; do not infer provider identity or switch accounts.

troubleshooting.problem: A nested lead has no dispatch tool or sufficient depth.
troubleshooting.solution: Use an authorized parent to dispatch selected specialist siblings and return results to the lead, or mark uncovered work incomplete. See references/host_setup.md.

documentation.support: Give the maintaining lead the exact package/source hashes, failed control or refusal and redacted evidence. Do not include credentials.

repository.text: One root skill with optional Claude Markdown and Codex TOML role assets. Host activation requires actual evidence.

testing.prepare: Keep private evidence outside source. Preserve the original 13 v1 controls and cases under evals/v1_cases.json. Freeze current evals/cases.json and evals/suite_cases.json before performing tasks. Actual observations, discovery and specialist returns remain separate from controls.
acceptance_criteria: Current mechanical suite passes; v1 preservation controls remain separately auditable.
Fresh performing tasks and public traces establish selected specialist behavior and lead synthesis.
Actual Claude Code and Codex runs are required before two-host acceptance; missing coverage stays incomplete.
improvement_steps: Locate a concrete failure, preserve its evidence and change only the responsible code or instruction.
Repeat affected controls and the same frozen behavioral task within the configured bounds.
